title: Buildkite Adds Scoped Secrets and New Agentic CI Tools
gist: Buildkite added pipeline-scoped secrets, new MCP tools for validating pipelines, comparing builds and repairing webhooks, Linux arm64 support in its GitHub Actions compatibility layer, and richer OpenTelemetry data in Agent v4.1.0. The release leans into AI coding agents as CI users.

insights.claim: Buildkite now lets engineers create cluster secrets restricted to the current pipeline, with optional conditions on branch, queue, build source or build creator, and values hidden after creation.
insights.speaker: Matt Mejia
insights.so_what: Narrower secret scoping reduces blast radius in CI/CD.
insights.quote: Pipeline secrets are cluster secrets restricted to the current pipeline, and branch, queue, build source, or creator conditions narrow access further.

insights.claim: Agent v4.0.9 redacts Buildkite tokens by prefix in job logs and v4.0.8 redacts captured job errors using secrets registered for the job, and the CLI adds a command for migrating GitHub Actions secrets.
insights.speaker: Matt Saunders
insights.so_what: Log redaction and migration tooling target credential leakage and GitHub Actions switchers.

insights.claim: Scoped storage does not remove the need to control secret use inside steps, and Buildkite documentation advises exposing a secret only to the steps that require it.
insights.speaker: Matt Saunders
insights.so_what: Secret exposure risk persists at step level regardless of storage scoping.

insights.claim: Buildkite's validate_pipeline MCP tool checks YAML syntax and structure against the official schema without uploading or building, but does not cover interpolation, plugin configuration, dependency references or dynamic steps.
insights.speaker: Matt Saunders
insights.so_what: Gives coding agents a cheap local feedback loop for CI config, though with known coverage gaps.
insights.quote: The check does not cover environment variable interpolation, plugin configuration, dependency references or dynamically generated steps.

insights.claim: The compare_builds tool diffs a failed build against the last successful build on the branch, reporting newly failing, recovered and still-broken steps with runtime and retry changes, and includes log tails for up to three newly failing steps.
insights.speaker: Matt Mejia
insights.so_what: Structured diagnostics reduce agent reliance on parsing full logs.
insights.quote: Log access alone does not debug a build.

insights.claim: Discrete validation, comparison and repair tools should reduce agent dependence on full-log parsing and low-level API calls, though webhook repair and pipeline creation still require careful permissions because they can modify CI configuration.
insights.speaker: Matt Saunders
insights.so_what: Agent-oriented CI APIs need least-privilege design.
insights.quote: Permissions remain important because webhook repair and pipeline creation can modify CI configuration.

insights.claim: After running evaluations Buildkite reversed an earlier default so failure summaries again include jobs that never ran, since making that optional led agents to issue extra tool calls; create_pipeline v1.23.0 now requires create_webhook, a breaking change.
insights.speaker: Matt Saunders
insights.so_what: Eval-driven tuning of tool defaults shows vendors treating agents as first-class API consumers.
insights.quote: with failure summaries now again including jobs that never ran

insights.claim: Remote MCP connections can be pinned to a single Buildkite organization via the server URL, and Test Engine execution traces and slowest-execution queries were added.
insights.speaker: Matt Saunders
insights.so_what: Org pinning limits cross-tenant agent mistakes.

insights.claim: Buildkite's GitHub Actions compatibility layer now runs on Linux arm64 agents, requiring explicit queue mapping for labels like ubuntu-24.04-arm with no fallback to x86-64 or emulation.
insights.speaker: Matt Saunders
insights.so_what: Lets arm64 CI fleets keep architecture parity when migrating Actions workflows.
insights.quote: do not fall back to x86-64 or emulation

insights.claim: The path-filter changed-file limit rose from 300 to 3,000 and more strategy.* values are exposed to expressions.
insights.speaker: Matt Saunders
insights.so_what: Large monorepos benefit from higher limits.

insights.claim: Agent v4.1.0 adds cache save and restore durations and sizes to telemetry and OpenTelemetry job spans now include commit, pull request and build author.
insights.speaker: Matt Saunders
insights.so_what: Richer CI telemetry helps diagnose slow jobs and retry patterns.

insights.claim: Elastic CI Stack v7 brings Agent v4 to AWS Linux and Windows instances, removes Agent v3 support and ends support for all Agent v3 releases on 3 September 2027.
insights.speaker: Matt Saunders
insights.so_what: Users on Agent v3 have a firm deadline.
insights.quote: Support for all Agent v3 releases ends on 3 September 2027.
insights.locator: The associated Elastic CI Stack v7
